global.title: Space exploration should learn from deep sea technology
global.summary: When the Artemis astronauts step onto the lunar surface, they will have spent considerable time and effort installing themselves in their bulky, heavy spacesuits. They will lumber onto the surface having limited mobility and time, struggling to accomplish their assigned tasks. Their activities will kick up clinging, razor-sharp lunar dust that they will invariably carry back into their capsule on their suits. And they will enter that capsule exhausted, perhaps even injured.

items.title: Crew-13 docking: Kutryk reaches station in under eight hours
items.summary: Canadian Space Agency (CSA) astronaut Josh Kutryk entered the International Space Station (ISS) on Thursday night, hours after NASA said his SpaceX Dragon capsule made the fastest trip to the orbiting laboratory by any U.S. spacecraft. The capsule, named Grace, docked with the forward port of the station’s Harmony module at 7:05 p.m. Eastern time. NASA put the trip from launch at seven hours and 55 minutes. The hatch then opened at 9:19 p.m. Kutryk floated in with NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins
